title: made my first mobile game with claude code and ai art in about 8 weeks. what worked and what didn't
author: th3strang3rr
selftext:
so this is my first mobile game, Critical Crossing. you control the traffic lights at one junction and every driver has a patience bar... calm ones wait, stressed ones creep forward, and the furious ones just go. the crash is on you.



since this sub is about the ai part, here's how i used it:



for the code, it's unity, mostly written with claude code. i made the design calls, did the testing and ran every build myself. it's really good at the code but it can't feel the game. that part was me playing it again and again, and my testers.



the art is all ai generated, in a pencil sketch style. generating wasn't the hard part, consistency was... getting the cars, the driver faces and the warden to look like one game, then fixing stuff at import (transparency, sizes, tinting).



for sound i tried ai sound effects first. they sounded ai, specially the whistle. ended up using real recordings from freesound.



the trailer and shorts were edited with claude from my unity recordings.



what ai didn't catch: bugs that only happen on a real phone. on my pixel, cars were running red lights that never happened once in the editor (frame rate thing). and the traffic light buttons... 7 testers said the default felt backwards so i flipped it. last week a friend told me the new default felt backwards to him too lol. so now i'm thinking of letting you just tap the road instead of a button.



it's free on android, no ads. would like to hear what you think. and if you've shipped something with ai art, did you get pushback for it?



link in the comments
